messages:
Maya K: quick snapshot — ran a focused comparison of L4 vs T4 vs A10G for two workloads: embeddings (512-d, short input) and small-chat (max_seq=256, interactive). summary below, attaching raw numbers from benchbot.

benchbot: results (us-west1 / eu-west1) — note: small-chat uses batch=1 streaming p50/p95, embeddings use batch=16 offline throughput.
```
EMBEDDINGS (512d, avg token len 30, batch=16)
- L4 (fp16):  avg qps 720, cost/unit $0.012/1k emb, p95 latency 45ms
- T4 (int8-gptq): avg qps 850, cost/unit $0.009/1k emb, p95 latency 60ms
- A10G (fp16 + kernel=flash_attn): avg qps 1300, cost/unit $0.020/1k emb, p95 latency 30ms

SMALL-CHAT (max_seq=256, batch=1 streaming)
- L4 (int8, kv-cache warm): p50=42ms, p95=210ms, tokens/sec ~75
- T4 (int8): p50=55ms, p95=260ms, tokens/sec ~60
- A10G (bf16 + flash kernels): p50=35ms, p95=95ms, tokens/sec ~140
```

Simon T: nice. key takeaway — T4 gives best cost for bulk embeddings when using gptq, but A10G crushes small-chat latency/throughput.

Liam Chen: region differences? any surprises in eu-west?

benchbot: eu-west1 numbers were ~6-12% lower throughput across GPUs vs us-west1. cause: slightly older CUDA/drivers on eu-west hosts + network latency for our eval harness. A10G gap narrowed for embeddings due to different kernel fallback (no flash in eu-west nightly).

Rachel P: kernel note — we saw flash_attn on A10G reduce p95 by ~2x for chat when seq>128. on L4/T4 we prefer fused_matmul kernels for int8 paths. logging: kernel selection was automatic via runtime heuristics.

Devon: quantization experiments? were you using nf4 or gptq int8? any quality regressions?

Maya K: embeddings used gptq int8 with symmetric quant — quality delta <0.5% cosine on our eval set vs fp16. small-chat used nf4-like quant for L4/T4; we ran a quick eval and saw subtle tokenization artifact in 2% of samples (mostly punctuation). flagged as minor but we should add regression tests.

Simon T: capacity sizing quick rules (based on these numbers):
- For 100k embeddings/day (burst to 10k/min): 1 T4 (with autoscale burst) is fine.
- For 1M embeddings/day: 2x T4 or 1x A10G (depends on latency requirement).
- For low-latency chat at 200 qps interactive: 2x A10G behind a routing policy, or 4x L4 with aggressive KV-cache + batching but expect higher p95.

Liam Chen: any kernel/regression to watch when we promote eu-west nightly to prod?

benchbot: yes — eu-west nightly lacks latest cudNN 9.1 micropatch so flash_attn falls back to slower kernels for A10G on some model shapes. we should pin runtime or build flash-attn fallback optimization. ticket created: #INF-2981.

Rachel P: ops checklist before rollout: verify driver versions, add kernel mismatch metric to console (flag when runtime uses fallback), and add a prompt set eval to catch the punctuation artifact in quantized chat.

Maya K: final recommendation for the short term:
- Embeddings-heavy customers: default to T4 with gptq int8 profile, enable batching=16 and prefix caching for repeated queries.
- Latency-sensitive chat: route to A10G (flash kernels) and use kv-cache + bf16 if model supports.
- For eu regions, add a canary that checks kernel selection & end-to-end p95 before full rollout.

Devon: awesome. will spin up a 24h canary in eu-west1 with both A10G and T4 pools and post Grafana links here. :thumbsup:

Maya K: thanks — attaching a link to the raw bench CSVs and the quick grafana snapshot (internal): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/bench/1793456789-snapshots

Simon T: outstanding — follow-ups: (1) INF-2981 driver/kernel fix (2) add quant regression test (3) update sizing doc with these numbers. i'll take (3).

Maya K: tagging product for visibility @Rachel P and @Devon.

Rachel P: noted, adding to next weekly eng-ml sync agenda.

benchbot: uploaded raw CSV: s3://redwood-bench/1793456789/bench-results.csv

Maya K: cool, closing thread once canary numbers in.
